title: Pole Position
description: Pole Position reached arcades in 1982 as a first-person Formula racing game in which players first run a qualifying lap and then race against the clock and rival cars on a grand-prix circuit. Players lined up to beat the clock, compare times with friends, and learn each course's corners by heart.
body:
Pole Position reached arcades in 1982 as a first-person Formula racing game in which players first run a qualifying lap and then race against the clock and rival cars on a grand-prix circuit. Players lined up to beat the clock, compare times with friends, and learn each course's corners by heart.

This tribute demo turns a race into a short text session: you choose accelerate, brake, or a lane change each tick, dodging obstacles and racing rival times. It is an original miniature inspired by the driving feel of Pole Position, not a copy of that game.

The fastest line is rarely the straightest one: brake before the obstacle, not on it, and change lanes early so speed stays up.
controls: Type accel, brake, left or right each tick, or quit to stop.

body:
Mario Kart Arcade GP reached arcades in 2005 as a kart racer built around a famous cast of characters, item boxes that swing races, and colorful courses full of shortcuts. Players lined up to beat the clock, compare times with friends, and learn each course's corners by heart.

This tribute demo turns a race into a short text session: you choose accelerate, brake, or a lane change each tick, dodging obstacles and racing rival times. It is an original miniature inspired by the driving feel of Mario Kart Arcade GP, not a copy of that game.

Saving a brake for the last stretch can rescue a run that started badly, since rivals' times are fixed and every second counts.
controls: Type accel, brake, left or right each tick, or quit to stop.
